questions.prompt: In OH's 7th District House race, outside money favors Democrats by $2.2M. Whose nominee has raised more?
questions.why: Outside money and candidate money point opposite ways here: the Republican leads fundraising by $1.5M.

questions.prompt: Groups helping Democrats have spent $718K in CA's 7th District House race. Are Democrats playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Democrats hold this seat now, so money helping Democrats here is defense.

questions.prompt: A party's coordinated spending in the last three weeks before Nov. 3 is disclosed when?
questions.why: Coordinated spending appears only on regular reports. Anything after Oct. 14 lands on the post-general report, due Dec. 3.

questions.prompt: Which race has drawn more outside money so far in the general election?
After NRSC v. FEC (June 2026), how much can a party spend in coordination with its Senate nominee?
options: Up to a set limit per state
questions.why: The Supreme Court struck down the limits on party coordinated spending, so parties can now spend without limit alongside their candidates.

questions.prompt: NO GOING BACK PAC INC. (a super PAC) has spent $1.3M in CO's 5th District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Republican or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: Can a corporation give unlimited money to a super PAC?
questions.why: Since Citizens United and SpeechNow.org (2010), corporations, unions and individuals can give super PACs unlimited sums.
